title: Cut the oil filter and drop the sump plate for debris forensics

notices.text: This is the single highest-information-per-hour task in the whole job. Cut the filter open with a filter cutter and spread the pleats on a white shop towel. Fine glittery ferrous paste on a magnet = IMS bearing wearing out. Shiny non-ferrous aluminium flake = bore scoring or piston skirt material. Brass/copper = bearing shells. Black rubbery chunks = chain ramp/guide plastic. Photograph the pleats and photograph the magnetic drain plug. Keep the debris in a labelled bag — it is your evidence for what the teardown should focus on.

steps.text: Cut the oil filter and drop the sump plate for debris forensics.

fasteners.name: Engine oil drain plug
fasteners.note: Always use a new aluminium crush washer. A magnetic drain plug is a worthwhile permanent upgrade.

sources.ref: Knowledge Gruppe, Fastening Specifications 996, p.15 item 23 (M18 x 1.5); WSM Gr.1 Part 1 (M96/01 edition) p.1-1, 03-1
